---
title: "Too Many Tools, Too Many Agents"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Who Said What. **Objective:** explain why a large toolset costs context and accuracy, and choose between a single call, a fixed workflow, an agent, and a plain script.
**Time:** about 20 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">Last verified (docs, not run): Claude API tool-search docs, Claude Code MCP docs and Anthropic's "Building effective agents" article on 2026-11-16 (sources in `research/fundamentals.md`). The figures quoted are Anthropic's own claims, not our measurements.</span>
Topics in this zone were inspired by Matt Pocock's course LLM Fundamentals (aihero.dev/llm-fundamentals). The explanations here are our own.
:::

Every tool you give an agent has a definition: a name and a description of how to use it. The model needs those definitions in its window to choose a tool. That is the cost this quest is about, followed by the related question of whether you need an agent at all.

## Tools cost context

Anthropic's tool-search docs say loading every tool definition up front causes context bloat. As an example they give a typical five-server setup that can use about 55 thousand tokens in definitions before any work starts. They also say Claude's ability to pick the right tool degrades once you exceed 30 to 50 available tools. These are Anthropic's statements on a docs page, with no method given, so treat them as a guide to the shape of the problem, not as measured thresholds.

The same docs describe **tool search**: keep most definitions out of the window and load a few on demand. They say it typically cuts that overhead by over 85 percent, and they advise it from about 10 tools upward, or when definitions are large. Below that, plain tool calling is better.

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

Per the docs, MCP tool search is on by default: only tool names and server instructions load at session start, and a full definition is fetched when needed. So extra MCP servers have a small effect on the window. It can be turned off with `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`, and on some older models it falls back to loading everything. Skills work the same way in spirit: only descriptions load at start. `/context` shows what takes space. Whether the 30 to 50 tool accuracy claim still applies behind deferral is not stated in the docs we read.

## OpenCode + Ollama

Not checked: whether OpenCode defers tool definitions. Assume tool definitions cost context until you know otherwise, and keep the set small, especially on a local model with a small window (general practice).

:::

The habit that follows (general practice, inferred from the above): few, clearly named tools, and remove the servers you do not use.

## Single call, workflow, agent, or script

Anthropic's article "Building effective agents" separates two things. A **workflow** orchestrates models and tools through paths fixed in code. An **agent** is a system where the model directs its own process and tool use. The article's advice is to start with the simplest solution that works, and it says that building no agentic system at all may be the right choice. For many uses, one well-prepared call is usually enough. It adds that agents trade speed and cost for performance, and that autonomy brings compounding errors, so test with limits: a **stopping condition** such as a maximum number of steps.

Our reading of that, as general practice:

- **A plain script** when the rule is known. Counting reads, converting a format, running fastqc then trim then align in a fixed order. A Nextflow pipeline is already a workflow.
- **A single call** when you paste the input and want a text answer, such as explaining an error.
- **An agent** when the next step depends on what it finds, such as debugging a failing run or exploring an unfamiliar repository. Even then, give it a way to check its own work and a limit.

Using none of these is also a fine decision.

<div data-ao-honour="tool-audit" data-xp="20">List the MCP servers and tools in your setup. For each, say when you last used it. Remove or disable one you do not need.</div>
<div data-ao-honour="script-first" data-xp="20">Take one task you gave an agent that had a known rule. Write down the script that would do it without a model.</div>
